correctness.rationale: Taking part sums S and repeating coordinates E gives F=E(J−I)S with S surjective, E injective and SE=D. The induced map on the part-constant subspace is B=(J−I)D, and the remaining quotient map is zero. For each residue a the group sum-zero subspace is acted on by −a; their direct sum is semisimple. The quotient on residue-group sums has dimension s≤p, with a zero column if s=p. Thus all nonzero irreducible degrees and the total nonzero generalized-eigenspace dimension of that quotient are at most p−1. Each B Jordan chain gains at most one over its primary quotient, and the vertex-space extension adds at most one at eigenvalue zero, none elsewhere. Nonzero blocks of length at most p have unipotent order dividing p, while the semisimple order divides L_p; the nilpotent part vanishes by step p+2. For equal residues, a=0 makes F square-zero of rank r−1_{r=1 mod p}. For a≠0, B=a(J−I) is scalar on the sum-zero space, with either a split constant line, a nilpotent rank-one perturbation when r=0 mod p, or a rank-r−1 image when r=1 mod p. In the rank-one perturbation case, taking the sum of a returning vector first forces (−a)^t=1 for a nonzero sum, then returning the vector forces p|t. The bijection on the image gives one recurrent preimage per fiber and p^(N−b)−1 transient ones. Coincident period labels are added; dividing by period gives the Euler factors for the zeta function.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks representative cases only. The uniform numerical cutoff is not asserted to be optimal.

No inspected passage supplies the quotient dimension and nonzero Jordan-chain bound here; an unrestricted finite linear map may have a nonzero Jordan block of length p+1 and thus a p²-divisible period.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General classification by a given endomorphism's elementary divisors is not a stronger assertion giving a part-count-independent constraint on those divisors. The residue-specific restriction is necessary.

value.rationale: The p² obstruction is uniform despite arbitrary growth in the graph and is false for general linear updates over the same field. The residue quotient explains the obstruction structurally. The exact common-residue law then identifies when a p factor can occur and supplies orbit counts and basin-entry counts, not only a period-existence assertion. These are natural invariants of this graph family; the usefulness does not depend on optimality of the coarse universal bound.
residual_risks: No exact census is given for arbitrary residues; no stronger uniform constants are credited.
